Last Mile Logistics Auditor¶

Delivery Performance Audit, Veridi Logistics¶

Dataset: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce | Tools: Python · Pandas · Seaborn · Matplotlib · Google Colab

Objective: Audit last-mile delivery performance across Brazil to identify the root causes of negative customer reviews, focusing on geographic disparities and seasonal delay patterns.

Key Results¶

  • 5 Northeast states (AL, MA, PI, CE, SE) show a critical late rate ≥15% against 5.9% in São Paulo

  • Super late deliveries drop the average review score from 4.29 to 1.79 / 5

  • Seasonal spikes identified: Black Friday (14.3%) , Carnival (16.0%) and March 2018 (21.4% peak)

  • Audited 96,478 delivered orders across 27 Brazilian states

Note: Some abbreviations are used throughout this study for readability:

  • Avg : Average
  • AL : Alagoas
  • MA : Maranhão
  • PI : Piauí
  • CE : Ceará
  • SE : Sergipe
  • RO : Rondonia
  • SP : São Paulo
  • CSV : Comma-Separated Values
  • ZIP : Zero Information Protocol
  • Cols : Columns
  • % : Percentage
  • vs : Versus
  • PT : Portuguese
  • EN : English
  • Peak : Highest recorded value
  • n : Number of orders
  • STDERR : Standard Error

Data Loading¶

Download the dataset from Kaggle - Olist Brazilian E-Commerce Dataset, extract the ZIP file, then upload the CSV files using the cell below.

Key Files:

  • olist_orders_dataset.csv : Central table
  • olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv : Customer sentiment
  • olist_customers_dataset.csv : Customer location
  • olist_products_dataset.csv : Product categories
  • product_category_name_translation.csv : Category translation (Portuguese to English)

Goal: Join Orders + Reviews + Customers into a single master dataset without duplicate rows.

Story 2: Delay Calculator, Real Delivery Performance¶

Formula: Days_Difference = order_estimated_delivery_date - order_delivered_customer_date

Value Meaning
≥ 0 days On Time
-5 to 0 days Late
< -5 days Super Late
In [109]:
df_delivered = df[df['order_status'] == 'delivered'].copy()

df_delivered['days_difference'] = (
    df_delivered['order_estimated_delivery_date'] -
    df_delivered['order_delivered_customer_date']
).dt.days

def classify_delivery(days):
    if days >= 0:
        return 'On Time'
    elif days >= -5:
        return 'Late'
    else:
        return 'Super Late'

df_delivered['delivery_status'] = df_delivered['days_difference'].apply(classify_delivery)

total = len(df_delivered)
summary = df_delivered['delivery_status'].value_counts()

print('Delivery Performance Summary')
for status, count in summary.items():
    pct = (count / total) * 100
    print(f'  {status}: {count:,} orders ({pct:.1f}%)')

print(f'\n Total late orders: {summary.get("Late",0) + summary.get("Super Late",0):,}')
print(f' Late rate: {((summary.get("Late",0) + summary.get("Super Late",0)) / total * 100):.1f}%')

In [114]:
import geopandas as gpd, requests, os

geojson_url  = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codeforamerica/click_that_hood/master/public/data/brazil-states.geojson'
geojson_path = 'brazil_states.geojson'

if not os.path.exists(geojson_path):
    r = requests.get(geojson_url, timeout=30)
    with open(geojson_path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(r.text)
    print('GeoJSON downloaded.')

brazil = gpd.read_file(geojson_path)

sigla_map = {
    'Acre':'AC','Alagoas':'AL','Amapá':'AP','Amazonas':'AM','Bahia':'BA',
    'Ceará':'CE','Distrito Federal':'DF','Espírito Santo':'ES','Goiás':'GO',
    'Maranhão':'MA','Mato Grosso':'MT','Mato Grosso do Sul':'MS','Minas Gerais':'MG',
    'Pará':'PA','Paraíba':'PB','Paraná':'PR','Pernambuco':'PE','Piauí':'PI',
    'Rio de Janeiro':'RJ','Rio Grande do Norte':'RN','Rio Grande do Sul':'RS',
    'Rondônia':'RO','Roraima':'RR','Santa Catarina':'SC','São Paulo':'SP',
    'Sergipe':'SE','Tocantins':'TO'
}
brazil['sigla'] = brazil['name'].map(sigla_map)

geo_status = df_delivered.groupby(['customer_state', 'delivery_status']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
geo_status['total']          = geo_status.sum(axis=1)
geo_status['on_time_pct']    = (geo_status.get('On Time',    0) / geo_status['total'] * 100).round(1)
geo_status['late_pct']       = (geo_status.get('Late',       0) / geo_status['total'] * 100).round(1)
geo_status['super_late_pct'] = (geo_status.get('Super Late', 0) / geo_status['total'] * 100).round(1)
geo_status = geo_status.reset_index()

brazil_merged = brazil.merge(geo_status, left_on='sigla', right_on='customer_state', how='left')

offsets = {
    'DF': ( 2.5, -2.5), 'SE': ( 3.0,  0.0), 'AL': ( 3.5,  0.5),
    'PB': ( 3.0,  1.0), 'RN': ( 3.0,  2.0), 'PE': ( 3.5, -1.0),
    'ES': ( 3.0, -1.5), 'RJ': ( 3.0, -2.5), 'SC': (-1.0, -2.5),
    'AP': ( 2.0,  2.0), 'RR': ( 0.0,  2.5),
}

def annotate_states(ax, brazil_merged, col):
    for _, row in brazil_merged.iterrows():
        if row.geometry is None or row['sigla'] is None:
            continue
        c   = row.geometry.centroid
        val = row.get(col, None)
        if val is None or pd.isna(val):
            continue

        label  = f"{row['sigla']}\n{val:.0f}%"
        sigla  = row['sigla']

        if sigla in offsets:
            dx, dy = offsets[sigla]
            xt, yt = c.x + dx, c.y + dy
            ax.annotate(
                label,
                xy=(c.x, c.y), xytext=(xt, yt),
                ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=6.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1a1a2e',
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color='#555555', lw=0.8),
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.2', fc='white', ec='none', alpha=0.7)
            )
        else:
            ax.annotate(
                label,
                xy=(c.x, c.y),
                ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=7, fontweight='bold', color='#1a1a2e',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.2', fc='white', ec='none', alpha=0.6)
            )

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(24, 11))

configs = [
    ('on_time_pct',    'On Time (%)',     'Greens',  'On Time Rate by State'),
    ('late_pct',       'Late (%)',        'Oranges', 'Late Rate by State'),
    ('super_late_pct', 'Super Late (%)' , 'Reds',    'Super Late Rate by State'),
]

for ax, (col, label, cmap, title) in zip(axes, configs):
    brazil_merged.plot(
        column=col, ax=ax, cmap=cmap, legend=True,
        legend_kwds={'label': label, 'shrink': 0.55, 'orientation': 'vertical'},
        edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.6,
        missing_kwds={'color': '#eeeeee'}
    )
    annotate_states(ax, brazil_merged, col)
    ax.set_axis_off()
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

plt.suptitle('Delivery Status by Brazilian State; Choropleth Maps\nVeridi Logistics Audit',
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('choropleth_map.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

Candidate's Choice 1: Seasonality Analysis¶

Business Value: Identifying seasonal patterns allows Veridi Logistics to proactively allocate resources during high-risk months such as Black Friday and Carnival to prevent delay spikes before they happen.

In [118]:
df_delivered['purchase_month'] = df_delivered['order_purchase_timestamp'].dt.to_period('M')

seasonality = df_delivered.groupby('purchase_month').agg(
    total_orders=('order_id', 'count'),
    late_orders=('delivery_status', lambda x: (x != 'On Time').sum())
).reset_index()

seasonality['late_pct'] = (seasonality['late_orders'] / seasonality['total_orders'] * 100).round(1)
seasonality['purchase_month'] = seasonality['purchase_month'].astype(str)
seasonality_clean = seasonality[seasonality['total_orders'] >= 100].copy()

ax.text(0, 8.5, 'Avg 8.1%', color='#2c3e50', fontsize=9)

months = list(seasonality_clean['purchase_month'])
idx_nov17 = months.index('2017-11')
idx_feb18 = months.index('2018-02')
idx_mar18 = months.index('2018-03')

ax.annotate('Black Friday', xy=(idx_nov17, 14.3), xytext=(idx_nov17-2, 19),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='black'), fontsize=9, ha='center')
ax.annotate('Carnival', xy=(idx_feb18, 16.0), xytext=(idx_feb18-2, 21),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='black'), fontsize=9, ha='center')
ax.annotate('PEAK 21.4%', xy=(idx_mar18, 21.4), xytext=(idx_mar18+1.5, 23),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#c0392b'), fontsize=10,
            color='#c0392b', fontweight='bold', ha='center')

ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.4)
ax.spines[['top', 'right', 'left']].set_visible(False)
ax.set_ylim(0, 27)
ax.set_xlabel('Month', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Late Delivery Rate (%)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Late Delivery Rate by Month, Seasonality Analysis\nVeridi Logistics Audit',
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=15)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('seasonality_analysis.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

Candidate's Choice 2: Review Score Distribution Deep Dive¶

Business Value: Understanding the full distribution of review scores reveals the severity of customer dissatisfaction and helps prioritize which delay threshold needs urgent action.

In [120]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))

statuses = ['On Time', 'Late', 'Super Late']
colors_map = {'On Time': '#27ae60', 'Late': '#e67e22', 'Super Late': '#c0392b'}

for i, status in enumerate(statuses):
    data = df_delivered[df_delivered['delivery_status'] == status]['review_score']
    score_counts = data.value_counts().sort_index()
    axes[i].bar(score_counts.index, score_counts.values,
                color=colors_map[status], edgecolor='white')
    axes[i].set_title(f'{status}\n(n={len(data):,})', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    axes[i].set_xlabel('Review Score', fontsize=10)
    axes[i].set_ylabel('Number of Orders', fontsize=10)
    axes[i].set_xticks([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
    axes[i].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.4)
    axes[i].spines[['top', 'right', 'left']].set_visible(False)
    avg = data.mean()
    axes[i].axvline(x=avg, color='#2c3e50', linestyle='--', linewidth=2)
    axes[i].text(avg+0.05, axes[i].get_ylim()[1]*0.9,
                 f'Avg: {avg:.2f}', color='#2c3e50', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

plt.suptitle('Review Score Distribution by Delivery Status\nVeridi Logistics Audit',
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('review_distribution.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

Key Findings Summary¶

Metric Value
Total Delivered Orders 96,478
On Time Rate 91.9%
Late Rate 8.1% (7,834 orders)
Worst State AL, Alagoas (23.9% late)
Best State RO, Rondonia (2.9% late)
Avg Review (On Time) 4.29 / 5
Avg Review (Late) 3.46 / 5
Avg Review (Super Late) 1.79 / 5
Peak Late Month March 2018 (21.4%)
Critical States (>=15%) AL, MA, PI, CE, SE

Conclusions¶

  1. Geographic disparity : Northeast states are systematically underserved: AL at 23.9% vs SP at 5.9%
  2. Delay drives dissatisfaction : Review scores collapse from 4.29 (On Time) to 1.79 (Super Late)
  3. Predictable seasonal spikes : Black Friday (14.3%), Carnival and March 2018 (21.4%) are recurring risk windows
  4. Not a nationwide failure : Southern states near São Paulo perform well below the 8.1% national average
